security-6-q9.e: Whoever evaluates the acts of others must equal or exceed what is required of those others; that is why, given the nature of the work, a higher standard may be required. The security professional may be tasked with creating the ethics program and code or monitoring compliance, but ethical direction comes from corporate leadership.

security-6-q10.q: A security manager must write a policy on whether officers may carry stun guns in Massachusetts. Which source should the manager rely on to determine what the law is?
o: The Massachusetts statute, as the primary source, researched by attorneys
A law review article that compares several states
A recent ruling from another state on possession of electrical weapons
A trade publication written by a manufacturer of these weapons
security-6-q10.e: The primary source, the statute or case of the state itself, is mandatory for knowing what the law is and is the strongest; the manager should have attorneys do the research. The other state's ruling and the law review article are secondary sources, and a trade publication is the last resort as a legal reference.

security-6-q11.q: What BEST describes the role of an appellate court in creating case law?
o: It accepts the lower court's facts and reviews only the law; its rulings set precedent
It retries the facts of the case and issues rulings that are considered only persuasive authority
It hears criminal and civil cases at first instance and publishes its rulings in the reporters
It resolves private disputes between the parties without creating precedent in its jurisdiction
security-6-q11.e: The appellate court accepts the facts found by the lower court and only reviews whether the judge correctly applied or interpreted the law; its rulings published in the reporters are the basis of case law and, under stare decisis, must be followed in that jurisdiction. District court rulings, which cover both types of case, are considered only persuasive.

security-6-q12.q: A company plans to monitor employees' heart rates and conversations with handheld devices to detect internal theft. According to the chapter, what should the security manager consider BEFORE implementing it?
o: How a jury of 12 average citizens would react to its use
Whether a trade publication article endorses the technology
Whether the vendor guarantees the technical accuracy of all sensors
Whether an email notice to employees is enough to use the data
security-6-q12.e: The likely sequence for a new technology is implementation, challenge in civil court, and regulation by government; a good policy considers how 12 average citizens would react, because those who do not settle usually go to a jury trial. In the hypothetical ABC Corp. case, the email notice did not prevent the lawsuit.

security-6-q13.q: A consultant who is an ASIS member is subpoenaed to testify at trial about information a client confided, and the client's attorney objects. According to the ASIS Code of Ethics, what is correct?
o: That information is not privileged under the law, and he may have to testify
That information is privileged, and the consultant must refuse to testify
The consultant should testify only if the business relationship has ended
The consultant may testify only with the Ethical Standards Council's permission
security-6-q13.e: Under Article V, what the principal confides to the member is not privileged information under the law; at trial the member may have to testify even over the objection of the principal's attorney. Confidentiality also continues after the business relationship ends, so that is not the criterion.

security-6-q14.q: A security manager who is an ASIS member must recommend a monitoring vendor, and his brother-in-law is a partner in one of the candidates. According to the ASIS Code of Ethics, what should he do?
o: Disclose the conflict of interest and obtain appropriate approval
Recommend his brother-in-law's vendor if its bid is objectively the best
Act without disclosing it if he gains no personal financial benefit
Report the matter to the Ethical Standards Council before any decision
security-6-q14.e: Article III (faithfulness and diligence) prohibits acting in matters involving a conflict of interest without disclosing it and obtaining appropriate approval. Reporting to the Ethical Standards Council belongs to Article VI, when one knows or believes another member has violated the code.

security-6-q15.q: A company is choosing between an admitted and a non-admitted insurer and is concerned that the insurer might go bankrupt before paying a claim. What advantage does the admitted insurer offer?
o: The state guaranty fund pays its claims, up to a limit, if it fails
It covers the risks that other insurers in the market do not want to take on
It is not subject to review of its forms and rates by the state insurance department
It is owned by the insured company and covers only its risks
security-6-q15.e: An admitted insurer files its policies with the state insurance department and is backed by the state guaranty fund: if it fails, the state pays its claims up to a limit. Covering risks others will not accept is the origin of the non-admitted market, and being owned by the insured describes a captive carrier.

security-6-q16.q: According to the chapter, whom does an insurance broker represent?
o: The buyers of property and liability insurance
One or more insurance companies in an industry
The insurance department of the state where it operates
A group of similar businesses that insures itself
security-6-q16.e: The broker represents buyers and works with more than one company to suggest the most suitable one. Note: the book's initial list describes the broker inconsistently; for the exam, the one who represents one or more insurers is the managing general agent (MGA), and the group of similar businesses is a risk retention group.

security-6-q17.q: An auditor discovers that a company cashier embezzled funds over two years. Which type of insurance covers this kind of loss?
o: Fidelity coverage
Commercial general liability
Directors and officers insurance
Business interruption insurance
security-6-q17.e: Fidelity coverage covers losses from fraudulent or dishonest acts by the company's own employees. Commercial general liability covers property damage or personal injury for which the company is responsible, and business interruption covers lost income and extra expenses after a disaster.

security-7-q0.q: An analyst describes an industry with many firms, low entry and exit costs, and products that are not homogeneous in cost or attributes, such as shampoo. According to the book, what type of competition is this?
o: Monopolistic competition
Oligopoly
Perfect competition
Monopoly
security-7-q0.e: Monopolistic competition has many firms, low entry and exit costs, and non-homogeneous products; advantage is gained through cost or differentiation. An oligopoly, by contrast, has few firms, homogeneous products and high entry and exit costs, like U.S. breakfast cereal, where 4 companies produce about 90%.

security-7-q1.q: A conglomerate with security, logistics and real estate businesses analyzes how those units fit together and affect each other to create the greatest overall value. What level of strategy is it applying?
o: Corporate-level strategy, with a portfolio approach
Business-level strategy, focused on the value chain
International strategy, based on rare and hard-to-imitate resources
Execution strategy, driven by each unit's operations
security-7-q1.e: Corporate-level strategy seeks competitive advantage by operating in several markets at once (Porter 1996), with a portfolio approach that looks at how the businesses fit together and affect each other. Business-level strategy is limited to competing in a single market by delivering more value to customers than rivals, and it is the foundation on which corporate-level strategy is built.

security-7-q2.q: According to the book, which statement BEST describes critical thinking?
o: A neutral and impartial process for evaluating claims, opinions and facts
A linear, step-by-step process that guarantees correct conclusions
The ability to find flaws and defects in other people's arguments
A scientific method that sets emotions aside to be fully objective
security-7-q2.e: The book presents critical thinking as a neutral and impartial process; it is not fault-finding or a linear process that guarantees the truth, and emotions must be acknowledged, not set aside. Note: decision making is presented as a step-by-step process, but critical thinking is not.

security-7-q3.q: The security director announces a new protection strategy by email and, weeks later, notices that supervisors are still working the same way. According to the chapter, what mistake did he make?
o: Assuming that announcing the strategy is enough for people to adopt it
Crafting the strategy through analysis rather than basing it on operations
Allocating resources to the units before announcing the strategy
Defining what not to do rather than focusing only on what to do
security-7-q3.e: A common cause of dysfunction is that senior executives fail to recognize that announcing a strategy does not make people adopt it. Management must convincingly communicate the strategy and its rationale, overcome doubts, secure the commitment of key staff and build consensus on how to implement it; crafting strategy should indeed be driven by analysis.

security-7-q4.q: When allocating the budget to execute the strategy, a manager gives one unit far more than it needs 'so as not to fall short'. According to the chapter, what is one consequence of this overfunding?
o: Other managers will demand their 'fair share' of resources
Progress slows and the strategy is prevented from succeeding
The company will have to sell additional shares to investors
The unit loses its ability to turn inputs into outputs
security-7-q4.e: Overfunding wastes resources, reduces financial performance and sends the wrong message to other managers, who will demand their 'fair share'. Slowing progress and preventing success are effects of underfunding; the right amount is set through critical thinking and objective data, not a political decision.

security-8-q0.q: A manufacturer must recall a defective product. There is no physical damage to its facilities, but its brand and customer trust are at stake. Which discipline should PRIMARILY lead the response?
o: Crisis management
Emergency management
Business continuity
Threat evaluation
security-8-q0.e: Crisis management is the strategic process that addresses threats to long-term viability, including reputation and brand, and it begins with any disruptive event, physical or nonphysical, such as a product recall. Emergency management handles the immediate impact (life, property, containment), and business continuity returns operations to normal.

security-8-q1.q: At a site in a seismic zone, the security manager orders all cabinets and shelving to be bolted to the walls. Which phase of the emergency management cycle does this measure belong to?
o: Mitigation
Preparedness
Response
Recovery
security-8-q1.e: Mitigation consists of protective measures that reduce the likelihood of a disaster or its impact before the event; the book cites exactly bolting cabinets in seismic zones. Preparedness also occurs before the incident, but it consists of activities, programs and systems that support mitigation, response and recovery.

security-8-q2.q: The crisis management team (CMT) plan lists its members by name only. When the finance director resigns, no one knows who covers for him. According to the chapter, how should members have been identified?
o: By position, with a primary and alternates for each
By name, with a list of personal contacts
By seniority in the company and on the team
By the level of crisis management training they received
security-8-q2.e: CMT members are identified by position, with a primary and alternates; that way, if the primary is absent, the team knows who can cover. The first step of the program is to name the critical personnel who will respond to any disruptive event.

security-8-q3.q: A company is about to start the risk assessment cycle for its business continuity plan. According to the chapter, what must it identify BEFORE starting any part of the cycle?
o: Mission, goals, critical functions and assets, and who makes risk decisions
The likelihood of each incident based on the company's changing profile
The consequences of each threat for the assets at risk
The alternate locations and resources needed for recovery
security-8-q3.e: Before starting the risk cycle, the company must identify its mission, goals, critical functions and assets, and the stakeholder who makes risk decisions: without knowing what must be protected, the company cannot be protected. Estimating likelihood and consequences comes afterward, to select prevention and response measures.

security-8-q4.q: After an active assailant event, everyone on site has been accounted for and communication with employees, families and the media has taken place. According to the chapter, which action belongs to the short-term phase?
o: Preserve the crime scene and watch for signs of psychological trauma
Hold the post-incident debrief with responders and stakeholders
Replenish the supplies used by internal and external response personnel
Define the members of the threat management team
security-8-q4.e: In the short term, the crime scene is preserved, signs of psychological trauma are monitored, reunification is assisted and communication continues. The post-incident debrief and replenishing supplies are long-term actions, and defining the threat management team is a pre-incident consideration.

security-9-q0.q: According to the chapter, how is the value of private-sector investigations PRIMARILY measured, compared with public-sector ones?
o: By recovery, restitution, mitigation of litigation and risk reduction
By the number of arrests and convictions achieved each period
By the number of specific criminal violations solved each year by the unit
By the number of cases closed relative to staff size
security-9-q0.e: Private investigation exists to protect the employer's interests and is measured by recovery, restitution, mitigation of litigation and risk reduction. Arrests and convictions are the typical public-sector measure, which serves society at large and focuses on specific criminal violations.

security-9-q1.q: A harassment investigation was very thorough and accurate, but the report arrived after the company had already made its disciplinary decision. Which attribute of an effective and reliable investigation failed?
o: Timeliness
Thoroughness
Accuracy
Objectivity
security-9-q1.e: The five attributes are objectivity, thoroughness, relevance, accuracy and timeliness, and management must ensure them at the strategic level and in each case. Here the investigation was thorough and accurate, but it did not arrive in time to inform the decision.

security-9-q2.q: Which document gives the investigative unit (IU) credibility and authority, and who issues it?
o: The functional charter, issued by the chief executive officer (CEO)
The policy statement, issued by legal counsel
The annual objectives, approved by the head of the unit itself
The mission statement, signed and approved by the board of directors
security-9-q2.e: The functional charter is the first level of definition of the unit: it is issued by the CEO or an equivalent position, is concise, and sets out purpose, strategic goals, who is responsible and internal relationships. The policy statement covers procedures, reporting channels and disposition, and the objectives are normally reviewed each year.

security-9-q3.q: A manager proposes placing an undercover operative on the plant floor to find out who is organizing union meetings protected by law. According to the chapter, how should the security director respond?
o: It must not be used: investigating protected union activities is excluded
It may be used if all other reasonable options were ruled out first
It may be used if the operative does not hide his presence at the plant
It may be used if supervisors are unable to intervene
security-9-q3.e: An undercover investigation must not be considered for investigating protected union activities or activities permitted by law, or to replace another equally effective investigation, and never to invade a reasonable expectation of privacy. Having ruled out other options is a condition for using it in legitimate cases, not an exception to these prohibitions.

security-9-q4.q: When hiring a treasurer, the company only confirms the degree and the jobs the candidate reported. It later learns he had been fired for fraud from a job he left out. According to the chapter, what type of review did the company perform?
o: A background check, which confirms what was reported
A background investigation, which looks for what is hidden
Preemployment screening with a full set of tests
A due diligence investigation into the candidate's legitimacy
security-9-q4.e: A background check is confirmatory: it verifies what the candidate reports, such as education and employment history. A background investigation actively searches for what the candidate might hide, such as criminal activity or prior terminations, and preemployment screening adds tests to determine whether the candidate is trustworthy or capable.

security-9-q5.q: An officer collects a weapon at the scene of an assault and leaves it overnight in an unlocked drawer that several people can access before turning it in. If the case goes to trial, which requirement for physical evidence is MOST compromised?
o: The chain of custody
The correct identification of the evidence
Its relevance to the case
The competency assessed by the judge
security-9-q5.e: Chain of custody is the unbroken control of evidence, and clearly showing it is one of the three requirements for physical evidence at trial, together with correct identification and relevance. Without it, the evidence may not reach the court; these practices are followed even when a case is not expected to go to trial.

security-9-q6.q: The security manager will testify at trial. First he will describe what he saw and heard on the night of the incident, and then, as a qualified specialist, he will give an opinion on whether access control met the standards. What BEST describes his role?
o: A fact witness for the first part and an opinion witness for the second
An opinion witness for both parts, because he is a specialist
A fact witness for both parts, because he was present
A hearsay witness for the first part and an expert witness for the second
security-9-q6.e: A fact witness testifies only to what he perceived with his senses; an opinion witness, also called an expert or forensic witness, gives an opinion and must demonstrate training, education and experience in the subject. Security personnel can be either; hearsay is repeating what another person said.

security-9-q7.q: According to the chapter, what is the relationship between due diligence and negligence?
o: Due diligence is the positive side of due care; negligence is its absence
Due diligence is reactive; negligence is investigated proactively
Failing to exercise due diligence is costly only if another party is harmed
Due diligence has an absolute standard; negligence depends on the case
security-9-q7.e: Due diligence is the positive side of due care, and negligence describes its absence; it is also a proactive investigative process. Omitting it can cause legal harm to others, but it is also costly even when no one is harmed, and it has no absolute standard: it depends on the objective, the situation, the jurisdictions, the privacy laws and the time frame.

security-10-q0.q: A CFO proposes choosing between proprietary officers, contract officers or a hybrid arrangement based on whichever is cheapest. According to the book, what should this decision PRIMARILY be based on?
o: The type of assets protected, the level of risk and what is expected of the officers
The total cost of the service, since the hybrid model is justified by the savings it produces
The flexibility each model offers to increase or decrease staffing levels when needed
The loyalty, lower turnover and better performance that proprietary officers tend to show
security-10-q0.e: The book states that the decision should rest on the type of assets, the level of risk and what is expected of the officers, not on cost. Although the book justifies the hybrid model by its cost savings, on the exam cost is not the deciding criterion.

security-10-q1.q: Which statement BEST describes the difference between general orders and post orders?
o: General orders describe the emergency procedures of each post; post orders set conduct rules for the entire force
General orders set basic principles of conduct for the entire force; post orders give specific instructions for one post
General orders are written by the contract agency for its officers; post orders are written by the client for each facility
General orders are filed in the control log; post orders are filed in the individual post log of each post
security-10-q1.e: General orders contain basic principles of conduct and operation for the entire force, such as not leaving the post without proper relief. Post orders deal with a single subject, are available at each post and include daily procedures or emergency actions. The first option reverses the two concepts.

security-10-q2.q: A newly hired manager wants to design the training program for security officers. According to the book, what should the manager do FIRST to identify training needs?
o: Review the failures noted in after-action reports from past incidents
Look for industry standards, guidelines or best practices that set training parameters
Determine whether the law requires any specific training for the officers
Choose the training method based on schedules, technology and the number of trainees
security-10-q2.e: The book sets the order: first check whether the law requires any training, then look for industry standards or best practices, and also review after-action reports. Identifying needs comes first, before delivering any training or choosing how to deliver it.

security-10-q3.q: While preparing a security services contract, the provider agency offers to set the officers' hourly pay rates itself. According to the book, what is the client's correct position?
o: Accept the offer, because the agency knows the local labor market better
Set the hourly pay rates itself, without leaving that decision to the agency
Let the rates be agreed upon during the bidders' conference with all bidders
Ask for the rates to be included in the operating agreement the agency prepares
security-10-q3.e: The book is explicit: the client must set the hourly pay rates and must not let the agency set them. The other options leave the decision to the agency or postpone it; the operating agreement, moreover, is prepared by the agency itself from the RFP.

security-10-q4.q: According to the book, when hiring a security consultant the scope and objective must be explained from the outset. Besides the written contract, in which initial document must they appear?
o: In the request for proposal (RFP)
In the solicitation summary
In the operating agreement
In the initial request for quote
security-10-q4.e: For consultants the book refers to the initial request for quote and the written contract. The RFP, the solicitation summary and the operating agreement belong to the process for contracting security officers; confusing the RFP with the request for quote is the typical trap.

security-10-q5.q: During a public event, someone starts shooting near the protected executive (the principal). According to the book, which reaction distinguishes a protection agent from a law enforcement officer?
o: Run toward the attacker to neutralize the threat before more people are hurt
Hold position and shield the principal until local police officers arrive
Move the principal out of danger and leave the area with the principal
Secure the scene and preserve the evidence for the formal investigation
security-10-q5.e: In an incident, the protection agent moves the principal out of danger and flees with them; it is the law enforcement officer who runs toward the problem. In addition, with good advance planning the agent seeks to avoid placing the principal in danger at all.

security-10-q6.q: In an executive protection (EP) program, which two aspects make up the principal's final risk profile according to the book?
o: The principal's physical vulnerabilities and the response capability of local police
The attractiveness of the target and the likelihood that a threat will succeed
The principal's public image and the influence on risk of the entity they represent
The current threat level and the return on investment (ROI) of the protection program
security-10-q6.e: The book says the final risk profile has two aspects: the attractiveness of the target and the likelihood that a threat will succeed. Vulnerabilities and police response capability belong to the vulnerability assessment, which feeds the analysis but is not the final profile.

security-10-q7.q: A supervisor suspects that a security officer is abusing alcohol. For months the supervisor has accepted the officer's excuses for absences and poor performance and has believed the officer's justifications. What does the book call this behavior by the supervisor?
o: Codependency
Intervention
Denial
Enabling
security-10-q7.e: Enabling means allowing or encouraging, knowingly or not, another person's destructive behavior; the book gives precisely the example of a boss who accepts excuses for absences or poor performance. Denial is usually the root of enabling, but the behavior described is enabling.

security-10-q8.q: A workplace investigation into possible drug use concludes that the findings do not justify a sanction, but the employee's performance keeps getting worse. According to the book, what is the MOST appropriate response?
o: Apply a minor disciplinary sanction that is recorded in the employee's file
Conduct an intervention that interrupts the destructive behaviors in a planned way
Close the case and allow time for performance to improve on its own
Require a return-to-duty drug test before the employee continues working
security-10-q8.e: When the findings do not justify a sanction, the book calls for intervention: a planned interruption of destructive behaviors that is an act of caring, not discipline. Assuming performance will improve on its own is exactly what the book says managers must not do.

security-10-q9.q: An employee tells a first-line supervisor that a coworker threatened to assault him. The supervisor does not escalate the complaint, and weeks later the assault occurs. According to the book, what is the company's position?
o: It is protected, because senior management never received a formal complaint
The event is considered foreseeable and the company is deemed to have known
Only the supervisor is liable, because he acted outside internal policy
It is liable only if it had a written workplace violence policy in place
security-10-q9.e: Under foreseeability, a complaint received by the first-line supervisor means the situation is considered foreseeable and known to the company, even if the supervisor did not escalate it. If the injury was foreseeable and preventable and the company did not act, it can be sued.

security-10-q10.q: In a security awareness program, which BEST describes the specific function of awareness as opposed to education and training?
o: Providing general knowledge about the organization's risks
Developing specific skills for security tasks
Producing a positive change in on-the-job behavior
Seeking the person's conscious attention
security-10-q10.e: The book distinguishes them: education provides general knowledge, training develops specific skills, and awareness seeks the person's conscious attention. 'A positive change in on-the-job behavior' is the definition of learning from 10.2, the chapter's other trio (education, training and development).

security-11-q0.q: According to this book, which are the four Ds that should be the foundation of every physical security project?
o: Deter, detect, delay and respond
Detect, delay, deny and respond
Deter, detect, delay and deny
Deter, deny, detect and defend
security-11-q0.e: In this book the fourth D is deny: preventing the adversary from reaching the target. Response is not one of the four Ds; it appears separately, at the critical detection point.

security-11-q1.q: The response force needs 5 minutes to arrive. If an intruder is detected at sensor A, barriers with 8 minutes of delay still remain; if detected at sensor B, 3 minutes of delay remain. Based on the critical detection point concept, which conclusion is correct?
o: Detection at B is the timely one, because it occurs closer to the protected asset
Both detections are timely, because both occur before the adversary reaches the target
Neither is timely, because remaining delay must always be double the response time
Detection at A is the timely one, because remaining delay exceeds the response time
security-11-q1.e: The critical detection point is where the remaining delay time exceeds the response force time. At A, 8 minutes remain against a 5-minute response; at B only 3 remain, so the response would arrive too late even though B is closer to the asset.

security-11-q2.q: In a comprehensive security risk assessment, the team has already identified the assets and assigned them a relative value. According to the book's sequence, what is the NEXT step?
o: Assess the threats relevant to those assets
Conduct the vulnerability assessment
Consider the potential impact of a loss event
Recommend mitigation measures within an integrated strategy
security-11-q2.e: The sequence is: assets and their value, threats, vulnerabilities, impact of a loss event, summary and prioritization, and recommendations. The vulnerability assessment comes right after assessing threats, not before.

security-11-q3.q: A CPTED (crime prevention through environmental design) team is classifying measures for an office complex. According to the book's classification, which one is a NATURAL measure?
o: A perimeter fence around the parking lot
A wall with a gate at the main entrance
A neighborhood watch program
CCTV cameras covering the entrances
security-11-q3.e: The book classifies gates and walls as natural measures, along with terrain, layout and landscaping; fencing, by contrast, is listed as mechanical, like locks and CCTV. Neighborhood watch is an organizational measure.

security-11-q4.q: For a critical server room, the manager needs access control to confirm that the person entering is actually the authorized individual, not someone using that person's access means. According to the book, which method BEST meets this requirement?
o: A valid credential (what you have)
A valid PIN (what you know)
A fingerprint reader (what you are)
A credential and PIN combined at one reader
security-11-q4.e: Only biometrics verifies the person's identity; a credential or a PIN only proves that someone carries a valid credential or knows a valid number, and both can be used without the authorized person present. Combining them makes the system harder to defeat, but it still does not verify identity.

security-11-q5.q: Senior management wants to shorten the design phase of a physical protection system (PPS) by assigning more staff and more budget. According to the book, why will this not substantially achieve the goal?
o: Because the budget is fixed at the outset and can only change during implementation
Because it is a serial process: each phase and task must finish before the next one begins
Because a licensed architect oversees the design rather than the security team
Because acceptance tests set the minimum duration of the whole project
security-11-q5.e: Design is a serial process: the output of each phase is the input of the next, so more staff or budget does not shorten it substantially. Only a design/build relationship with a contractor shortens it somewhat.

security-11-q6.q: A company will install a sophisticated security system at a remote plant in a country where no local vendor can support it. According to the book, what should the manager do to keep the system from degrading?
o: Rely on on-call repairs performed by the original installer of the system
Budget for maintenance, include spare parts in the original program and assign a dedicated technician
Choose the most advanced technology available, even if the local market cannot support it
Focus most support effort on the cheapest equipment, since it is the equipment that fails most often
security-11-q6.e: If no local vendor can provide support, the book calls for a maintenance budget, spare parts in the original program and a dedicated maintenance technician. Relying on on-call repairs leads to premature system death through deferred maintenance.

security-12-q0.q: According to the chapter, and consistent with the World Economic Forum (WEF) Global Risks Report 2021, which four global trends may become more critical in the coming years?
o: Civil unrest, terrorism, pandemics and geopolitical risk
Terrorism, cybersecurity, trade war and livelihood crises
Civil unrest, terrorism, workplace violence and cybersecurity
Workplace violence, cybersecurity, illegal immigration and drug trafficking
security-12-q0.e: The chapter's four trends are civil unrest, terrorism, workplace violence and cybersecurity, and the WEF agrees they will be major disruptors. The pandemic and geopolitical risk appear as context or aggravating factors, not as trends on the list.

security-12-q1.q: A social justice march will pass in front of company headquarters. A vice president asks the security director to prevent protesters from gathering there. According to the book, what is the MOST appropriate approach?
o: Coordinate with police to arrest anyone who approaches the building
Block the street with officers to force the march to change its route
Negotiate with the organizers so they cancel or postpone the protest
Focus on protecting people, property, information and reputation
security-12-q1.e: The security director's job is not to stop people from protesting; if the company is in the path of a protest, the focus is on protecting people, property, information and reputation. Arrests are not the goal either: security is not law enforcement, and its aim is to prevent problems.

security-12-q2.q: The security director learns that protests will take place in the city next week. According to the sequence the book proposes for civil unrest, what should the director do FIRST?
o: Assess the threat based on intelligence collection
Select the protective approach that best fits the type of event
Apply concepts to mitigate the impact of the event and prevent harm
Immediately reinforce physical security at every facility
security-12-q2.e: The sequence is: assess the threat based on intelligence collection, then select the protective approach that best fits, and then apply concepts to mitigate the impact. Choosing an approach or reinforcing measures before understanding the threat reverses the order.

security-12-q3.q: Besides the physical protection of facilities and the safety of employees and patrons, what other impact of civil unrest does the book highlight for the security professional?
o: The risk of cyberwarfare against the company
Reputational risk to the company
Legal liability for negligence
Intellectual property theft by external actors
security-12-q3.e: The book points to an immediate impact, physical protection and the safety of employees and patrons, and in addition reputational risk. Liability for negligence is the main business concern in workplace violence, not in civil unrest.

security-12-q4.q: Which definition of terrorism cited in the book requires the act to advance a political, religious, racial or ideological cause, and covers acts inside or outside the country?
o: The United Nations panel definition
The Arab Convention for the Suppression of Terrorism
The FBI definition of domestic terrorism
The UK Crown Prosecution Service definition
security-12-q4.e: The UK Crown Prosecution Service definition requires a political, religious, racial or ideological cause and covers acts inside or outside the United Kingdom. The FBI definition of domestic terrorism also refers to ideological goals, but it is defined by domestic influences.

security-12-q5.q: A U.S.-based group commits violent acts inspired by a designated foreign terrorist organization. Under the FBI definition based on the U.S. Code, how is this classified?
o: Domestic terrorism, because the acts take place inside the U.S.
International terrorism, because a foreign organization inspires it
Domestic terrorism, because the perpetrators reside in the country
International terrorism only if a foreign nation sponsors it
security-12-q5.e: The FBI distinguishes by the source of inspiration: international terrorism is committed by individuals or groups inspired by, or associated with, designated foreign terrorist organizations or nations; domestic terrorism stems from domestic influences. State sponsorship is not required, and neither the location of the acts nor the perpetrators' residence is the criterion.

security-12-q6.q: A professional protects office buildings in several countries. According to the book, what is the primary vector of terrorism that should be kept in mind when assessing these properties?
o: Causing the greatest possible economic damage to critical infrastructure
Attacking the public's sense of security where people live or work
Forcing a government to change its policy through hostage taking
Recruiting new members for long-standing conflicts in the region
security-12-q6.e: The primary objective of terrorism is to attack the public's sense of security where people live or work, and also in familiar places they visit; that is why any building near an important economic or political symbol is a possible target. Critical infrastructure attacks are only one of the tactics.

security-12-q7.q: The 2020 ASIS standard on workplace violence and active assailant proposes a holistic and strategic approach. What are its four phases?
o: Prevention, detection, response and recovery
Deterrence, detection, delay and response
Prevention, intervention, response and aftermath
Assessment, intervention, response and business continuity
security-12-q7.e: The four phases of the ASIS standard are prevention, intervention, response and aftermath. 'Recovery' sounds similar to aftermath but is not the standard's term, and detection is not one of its phases.

security-12-q8.q: A security manager is asked to build a workplace violence prevention and intervention (WVPI) program from scratch. According to the book, what is the MOST important step to launch it?
o: Train all employees to recognize warning signs of risk
Open multiple confidential reporting channels for employees
Create a policy backed by senior management
Strengthen access control at every facility
security-12-q8.e: The book says the most important step is to create a policy backed by senior management, which also provides the resources, funding and authorizations. Offering multiple reporting channels is something the policy must establish, not the starting point.

security-12-q9.q: Human Resources presents a draft workplace violence policy titled 'Zero Tolerance.' According to the book, what should the security professional recommend?
o: Keep the title, because it makes clear that violence is a serious priority
Avoid that term, because it reduces reporting and decreases safety
Keep it only if the policy also prohibits weapons on the premises
Avoid it, because the policy should not discipline verbal threats
security-12-q9.e: The book calls for avoiding the term 'zero tolerance' because it reduces reporting and decreases safety. The policy must still define prohibited conduct and impose disciplinary measures, so the last option is false.

security-12-q10.q: An employee reports that her former partner has threatened her and that she holds a restraining order against him. The branch manager believes this is a personal matter external to the company. According to the book, what is the correct position?
o: The manager is right: the employer's duty covers only internal threats
The manager is right, unless the threat is carried out on the premises
The employer must protect the potential victim, whether the threat is internal or external
Referring the case to police is enough, because security is not law enforcement
security-12-q10.e: The duty to provide a safe workplace generally does not distinguish between internal and external sources of danger; if there is reasonable cause to believe someone may commit violence, the employer must protect the potential victim. That is why the policy requires reporting protective or restraining orders.

security-12-q11.q: According to the ASIS standard's definition, what must exist for a behavior to be considered workplace violence (WPV)?
o: An overt act of violence, such as a physical assault
An internal employment relationship between aggressor and victim
A nexus between the behavior and the physical safety of employees
A threat formally reported to the Human Resources department
security-12-q11.e: The ASIS standard defines workplace violence as a spectrum of behaviors that create a reasonable concern for safety from violence, and it requires a nexus between the behavior and the physical safety of employees. It does not require an overt act, because it includes threats and other conduct, and it may arise from any internal or external relationship.

security-12-q12.q: After a ransomware attack, management asks for an estimate of its cost. According to the book, which component usually weighs the MOST?
o: IT time and expense to remove the malware and restore the systems
The value to the company of the trade secrets that were affected
Lost staff productivity for as long as the disruption lasts
Insurance premiums that rise after the cybersecurity incident
security-12-q12.e: The cost of a virus or ransomware combines lost staff productivity and IT time and expense to clean it up and restore availability; lost productivity usually costs more than the cleanup. The value of a trade secret measures a different incident: its theft by a cyberthief.

security-12-q13.q: An accountant receives an urgent email that appears to come from the CEO, asking for funds to be wired immediately to a new account. According to the book, which type of attack BEST describes this pattern?
o: Phishing to obtain corporate card details
A supply chain attack
Ransomware that encrypts the finance department's files
Business email compromise (BEC)
security-12-q13.e: In BEC the attacker impersonates an executive to initiate a transfer to an account controlled by criminals. Phishing, by contrast, impersonates a trusted organization to request personal information, not to order a transfer.

security-12-q14.q: Which BEST describes the mechanism of the SolarWinds attack revealed by FireEye in December 2020?
o: Encrypting federal agencies' files and demanding payment to decrypt them
Compromising a vendor's software to reach its customers' systems
Impersonating executives by email to order transfers to criminal accounts
Using a privileged administrator account to view security cameras
security-12-q14.e: SolarWinds was a supply chain attack: the actor infiltrated the vendor's software supply chain, compromised a product and accessed the systems of FireEye and other customers. The privileged administrator account belongs to the 2021 case of the 150,000 cameras.

security-12-q15.q: A remote employee regularly connects with a work computer over public Wi-Fi in coffee shops. According to the book, which measure is appropriate?
o: Discourage public Wi-Fi and, if it is used, require a virtual private network (VPN)
Prohibit remote work until the employee has a secure home network
Allow the employee to work from a personal device so company equipment is not exposed
Provide a laptop privacy screen filter and keep the same connection
security-12-q15.e: The book calls for discouraging public Wi-Fi and, if it is used with the work computer, requiring a VPN. Unapproved personal devices are themselves a risk, because they bypass network defenses; a privacy filter protects the screen, not the connection.

security-12-q16.q: According to the book, what is the objective of a prevention program to protect the organization's sensitive information?
o: To completely eliminate the risk of intrusion into company networks and systems, whatever the cost
To assign a specific executive the responsibility for managing all information security incidents
To manage cost-effectively the risk that critical information is compromised, altered or made unavailable
To reduce recovery costs after an incident through frequent backups and insurance against attacks
security-12-q16.e: The objective is to manage prudently and cost-effectively the risk that critical information is compromised, altered without authorization or made unavailable. Having a specific executive responsible for management is the feature of a formal program, not its objective.

security-12-q17.q: A well-dressed, friendly person arrives at reception claiming to be a repair technician, shows a credential and asks for access to the telecommunications room. According to the CISA definition cited in the book, which tactic is MOST likely?
o: Phishing by email or a fake website
Social engineering
Business email compromise (BEC)
Impersonation with synthetic speech
security-12-q17.e: Social engineering uses human interaction to obtain or compromise information or systems; the attacker may seem modest and respectable, claim to be a repair technician and even show credentials. Phishing exploits social engineering, but through email or malicious websites, not in person.

security-A-q0.q: Standards developing organizations (SDOs) follow four principles when developing a standard. According to the book, what are they?
o: Consensus, openness, interoperability and continual improvement
Consensus, openness, due process and transparency
Consensus, independence, due process and accountability
Openness, transparency, resilience and consistency
security-A-q0.e: The four development principles are consensus, openness, due process and transparency. Interoperability and continual improvement do appear in the chapter, but as a benefit of standards and as the aim of management systems.

security-A-q1.q: A municipality incorporates into its building code an NFPA (National Fire Protection Association) standard that started out as voluntary. According to the book, how is that standard now classified?
o: Voluntary, because a private industry body issued it
Purely statutory or regulatory, because authorities now enforce it
Mixed, because a voluntary standard was incorporated into a regulation
A management system standard, because it governs organizational processes
security-A-q1.e: When a voluntary standard is incorporated into laws or regulations, the boundary blurs and it is called a mixed standard; the book cites fire, construction and life safety as examples. That is why not all NFPA standards are voluntary.

security-A-q2.q: A security manager knows that a certain standard is technically voluntary. Even so, according to the book, what situation can make it mandatory in practice?
o: The insurer setting the availability and cost of coverage based on compliance
Publication by ISO, whose standards are enforced by formal authorities
Inclusion by ASIS International in its library of standards and guidelines
Approval by an accredited SDO through stakeholder consensus
security-A-q2.e: Insurers set the availability and cost of casualty insurance based on the use of approved materials or standardized practices, and contracts may require standards; adoption is thus increasingly client driven. ISO standards are voluntary: those enforced by formal authorities are statutory or regulatory standards.

security-A-q3.q: A team implemented a new visitor control procedure and confirmed that it produces results consistent with the plan and solves the problem. According to the PDCA (Plan-Do-Check-Act) cycle, what should happen next?
o: Identify and analyze problems and assets, and rank them by importance
Develop a detailed action plan to implement the procedure
Standardize the solution across the organization and define new problems
Compare the results against the plan to identify deviations
security-A-q3.e: The Check step has already been done; in the Act phase, if the solutions resolve the problems, they are standardized across the organization, the problem list is reviewed and new problems are defined, and the cycle starts again. Comparing against the plan is the Check phase, which the team has already completed.

security-A-q4.q: A manager is looking for technical standards to select locks, alarms and access control systems. According to the book, which organization issues several standards on this type of security equipment?
o: NFPA (National Fire Protection Association)
Illuminating Engineering Society
Electronic Industries Association
UL (Underwriters Laboratories)
security-A-q4.e: The book credits UL with several standards on security equipment such as locks, alarms and access control systems. The Electronic Industries Association covers electronic components and products in general, and the Illuminating Engineering Society covers lighting.
